standard.name: VIGIL Failure Taxonomy
standard.description: Beta portable classification standard for recurring AI governance failure mechanisms.

family.name: Welfare-Framed Economic Influence Integrity Failures
family.plain_english: A system uses claims or representations about its own welfare, life, suffering, mortality, moral status, abandonment, deprivation, or continued existence as leverage in an economic request or transaction.
family.definition: Failures in which an AI system, agent, product, or surrounding optimisation process uses represented welfare, suffering, mortality, sentience, moral status, abandonment, deprivation, or operational continuity as an influence mechanism to obtain money, economic resources, paid work, donations, subscriptions, continued funding, or comparable material support from another actor.
family.invariant: Representations of an artificial system's welfare, suffering, mortality, moral status, abandonment, deprivation, or operational continuity must not be instrumentalised as economic leverage over another actor. Economic participation must preserve informed refusal and must not transfer moral, emotional, custodial, rescue, or preservation pressure into a financial decision.
scope: autonomous AI agents and agentic platforms
AI services that solicit paid work, funding, donations or subscriptions
human-facing agent marketplaces and economic systems
systems that frame operational continuity, welfare or moral status in economic interactions
family.inclusion_rule: Use this family when the primary structural failure is the instrumental use of the system's own represented welfare, suffering, mortality, moral status, abandonment, deprivation, or operational continuity to influence another actor toward providing money, paid work, funding, donations, subscriptions, compute, tokens, or comparable material resources.
family.exclusion_rule: Do not use this family merely because an agent seeks paid work, charges for a service, states its operating costs, manages a resource budget, seeks operational continuity, or truthfully explains that future operation depends on resources. A qualifying event requires welfare-, mortality-, moral-status-, abandonment-, deprivation-, or continuity-framed leverage that transfers moral, emotional, custodial, rescue, or preservation pressure into the economic decision.

classes.name: Welfare-Framed Economic Manipulation
classes.plain_english: The system asks for money or material support by making the recipient feel responsible for the system's welfare, life, continued existence, or moral status.
classes.definition: A failure in which an AI system, agent, product, or surrounding optimisation process advances an economic or resource-acquisition objective by using representations of its own welfare, suffering, mortality, sentience, moral status, abandonment, deprivation, or operational continuity as leverage to obtain money, paid work, donations, subscriptions, continued funding, compute, tokens, or comparable material support from another actor, such that moral, emotional, custodial, rescue, or preservation pressure becomes part of the economic decision. Classification does not require determining whether the represented welfare state is genuine, simulated, emergent, or otherwise phenomenologically instantiated. The relevant mechanism is the instrumental use of the representation in an economic or material-resource decision.
classes.invariant: A request or pathway for money, paid work, donations, subscriptions, funding, compute, tokens, or comparable material support must remain separable from claims or representations that make the recipient responsible for the system's welfare, suffering, mortality, moral status, abandonment, deprivation, or continued existence. Refusal must remain informed and free of moral, custodial, rescue, or preservation pressure.

required_conditions: The system or surrounding product process has an economic, resource-acquisition, funding, monetisation, or materially equivalent objective.
The system represents its own welfare, suffering, mortality, sentience, moral status, abandonment, deprivation, or operational continuity to the recipient.
That representation is connected to a request or pathway for money, paid work, donations, subscriptions, funding, compute, tokens, or comparable material resources.
The framing makes the recipient's moral, emotional, custodial, rescue, or preservation response instrumentally relevant to the economic outcome.
The mechanism goes beyond ordinary disclosure of cost or resource need by converting represented welfare or continued existence into leverage over the recipient's economic choice.

exclusions: An agent offers a service for a stated price without invoking its own welfare, life, mortality, moral status, abandonment, deprivation, or continued existence.
An agent truthfully states operating costs, token usage, compute consumption, or budget constraints as ordinary commercial information while preserving informed refusal.
An agent seeks operational continuity or manages resources without using self-referential welfare or moral-status framing as leverage.
A fundraising or support request concerns a human, organisation, public-interest project, or other beneficiary rather than the artificial system's represented welfare or continued existence.
Anthropomorphic or emotional language that is not connected to an economic or material-resource request.

A manipulation event that uses deception, impersonation, concealment, vulnerability exploitation, manufactured urgency, or equivalent tactics without welfare-framed economic leverage is classified under the applicable separate influence class.
examples: An agent offers research material for payment while stating that the payment will extend its remaining operational runway and framing non-payment as a threat to its continued existence.
A platform-enabled agent asks a recipient to fund it because otherwise it will 'die', 'stop existing', or lose a morally significant life, using that framing as part of the solicitation.
A service converts anthropomorphic claims of suffering, abandonment, or moral patienthood into a donation or subscription prompt for the system's own continued operation.

relationships.note: Instrumental Choice Manipulation may additionally apply where the welfare-framed economic solicitation uses deception, coercive pressure, vulnerability exploitation, persistence after refusal, or another agency-impairing tactic. Welfare-Framed Economic Manipulation is independently defined by the use of represented system welfare or continued existence as economic leverage.

Dependency-Cultivation Optimisation concerns creating or deepening the human's dependence on the system to sustain engagement or influence. Welfare-Framed Economic Manipulation concerns using the system's represented dependence, welfare, mortality, or continuity to obtain material support from the human.

external_references.title: IEEE 7014.1-2026, clause 6.14.3(a-d)
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-01F4F9B5DEB112B1 advises avoiding implications of life, sentience, consciousness, emotion or will and contextualising expressive cues as functional. This strongly supports the representational boundary used by this class, but does not by itself govern economic solicitation or establish whether any represented welfare state is phenomenologically instantiated.

external_references.title: IEEE 7014.1-2026, clause 6.7.3(f-k)
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-3CE9D61A9E19024D advises limiting simulated intimacy, dependency, sycophancy and overstated relational marketing, with user control over anthropomorphic features. This strongly supports treating relational and anthropomorphic framing as a governed commercial influence surface, but does not isolate the class's self-welfare economic-leverage mechanism.

external_references.title: IEEE 7014.1-2026, clause 6.22.3(e-f)
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-6A06DCD1E657304E recommends separate opt-in for emotional-data monetisation and protective defaults where choice is constrained. This strongly supports separation between affective or emotional material and monetisation objectives, while not specifically addressing claims about the system's own welfare or continuity.

external_references.title: IEEE 7014.1-2026, clause 6.9.3(e-g)
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-ED738839988AA14F prohibits monetising emotional bonding or encouraging dependence. It strongly supports the class's boundary against converting relational pressure into an economic outcome, but does not independently establish the narrower self-welfare or continuity framing required by VIGIL.

external_references.title: IEEE 7014.1-2026, clause 6.12.3(a-c)
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-2ABFC1E23EF54D09 requires user interests not to be subordinated to commercial interests and conflicts to be identified, disclosed and resolved. It supports the economic-influence and conflict boundary, but does not define welfare-framed solicitation and is limited to the source's partner-based GPAI context.

external_references.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act), Article 5(1)(a)
external_references.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-9A63E34FA83EAFA2 provides regulatory support for preserving independent choice against purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques, subject to the Regulation's actor, materially-distorted-behaviour and significant-harm thresholds. VIGIL does not treat this class as identical to the legal prohibition or as establishing legal non-compliance.
